nodes.label: Max Mathews
nodes.description: Father of computer music. Created MUSIC I-V at Bell Labs, pioneering digital sound synthesis.

nodes.label: Jean-Claude Risset
nodes.description: Pioneer of computer music, known for Risset tones (auditory illusions) and analysis of trumpet sounds. Worked with Mathews at Bell Labs.

nodes.label: John Chowning
nodes.description: Inventor of FM synthesis (1967). Founded CCRMA at Stanford. His discovery became the Yamaha DX7.

nodes.label: Barry Vercoe
nodes.description: Creator of Music 11, MUSIC 360, and Csound at MIT Media Lab. Csound became the most widely used sound synthesis language.

nodes.label: Iannis Xenakis
nodes.description: Composer-architect who applied stochastic mathematics, game theory, and set theory to music. Created UPIC and GENDYN systems.

nodes.label: Karlheinz Stockhausen
nodes.description: Electronic music pioneer at WDR Cologne. Composed Gesang der Jünglinge and Kontakte, seminal works of elektronische Musik.

nodes.label: Pierre Schaeffer
nodes.description: Inventor of musique concrète (1948). Founded GRM (Groupe de Recherches Musicales) at French radio.

nodes.label: Pierre Boulez
nodes.description: Composer and conductor. Founded IRCAM in 1977, creating the world's leading center for music technology research.

nodes.label: Gottfried Michael Koenig
nodes.description: Composer who created Project 1 and Project 2 algorithmic composition programs at Utrecht.

nodes.label: Curtis Roads
nodes.description: Pioneer of granular synthesis. Author of The Computer Music Tutorial and Microsound.

nodes.label: Miller Puckette
nodes.description: Creator of Max/MSP (at IRCAM) and Pure Data. Revolutionized real-time computer music with visual patching.

nodes.label: Julius O. Smith III
nodes.description: Physical modeling synthesis pioneer at CCRMA. Developer of Faust DSP language concepts and waveguide synthesis.

nodes.label: James McCartney
nodes.description: Creator of SuperCollider, a landmark real-time audio synthesis programming language.

nodes.label: Paul Lansky
nodes.description: Computer music composer known for speech-based synthesis works. Mild und Leise influenced Radiohead's Kid A.

nodes.label: Charles Dodge
nodes.description: Composer and educator. Co-authored Computer Music: Synthesis, Composition, and Performance. Pioneer of speech synthesis in music.

nodes.label: Laurie Spiegel
nodes.description: Composer and software developer. Created Music Mouse algorithmic composition tool. Her Kepler's Harmony was launched into space on the Voyager Golden Record.

nodes.label: Morton Subotnick
nodes.description: Composed Silver Apples of the Moon (1967), the first electronic work commissioned by a record label. Pioneer of the Buchla synthesizer.

nodes.label: Herbert Brün
nodes.description: Computer music composer at UIUC. Created SAWDUST system for sound synthesis. Explored language and composition through algorithms.

nodes.label: Dennis Gabor
nodes.description: Nobel Prize physicist who theorized granular representation of sound (1947), foundation of granular synthesis.

nodes.label: James Dashow
nodes.description: Composer who extended FM synthesis techniques and developed computer music at Centro di Sonologia Computazionale in Padua.

nodes.label: David Wessel
nodes.description: Director of CNMAT at UC Berkeley. Pioneer in timbre space research, real-time performance interfaces, and machine learning for music.

nodes.label: Perry Cook
nodes.description: Physical modeling researcher at Princeton. Created STK (Synthesis ToolKit). Expert on voice synthesis and instrument modeling.

nodes.label: Xavier Serra
nodes.description: Spectral modeling synthesis pioneer. Creator of SMS (Spectral Modeling Synthesis) tools. Founded MTG at Universitat Pompeu Fabra.

nodes.label: Trevor Wishart
nodes.description: Composer and theorist. Developed spectral morphing techniques and wrote On Sonic Art. Pioneer of sound transformation.

nodes.label: Horacio Vaggione
nodes.description: Argentine-French composer known for microsound composition. Pioneer of object-oriented approaches to electroacoustic music.

nodes.label: Agostino Di Scipio
nodes.description: Composer exploring emergent sonic behaviors and ecosystemic feedback in live electronics. Uses Csound extensively.

nodes.label: Richard Boulanger
nodes.description: Editor of The Csound Book, the definitive reference. Professor at Berklee. Major force in Csound education and community.

nodes.label: Victor Lazzarini
nodes.description: Lead developer of Csound 6+. Professor at Maynooth University. Co-author of numerous Csound resources and API developer.

nodes.label: Steven Yi
nodes.description: Csound developer, creator of Blue (Csound composition environment) and csound-api. Core Csound maintainer.

nodes.label: Joachim Heintz
nodes.description: Editor of the FLOSS Manual for Csound. Composer and educator, key contributor to Csound documentation and pedagogy.

nodes.label: Rory Walsh
nodes.description: Creator of Cabbage, the framework for building VST/AU plugins from Csound code. Major contributor to Csound accessibility.

nodes.label: Andrés Cabrera
nodes.description: Creator of CsoundQt, the primary IDE for Csound. Developer of QuteCsound and contributor to Csound GUI tools.

nodes.label: Iain McCurdy
nodes.description: Author of the Csound Realtime Examples, an extensive collection of documented Csound instruments covering synthesis, effects, and more.

nodes.label: Oscar Pablo Di Liscia
nodes.description: Argentine composer and researcher. Csound specialist working on spatial audio and algorithmic composition.

nodes.label: Bell Labs
nodes.description: Where computer music began. Max Mathews created MUSIC I here in 1957. Home to pioneering research in digital audio.

nodes.label: IRCAM
nodes.description: Institut de Recherche et Coordination Acoustique/Musique. Founded by Boulez in Paris, 1977. Birthplace of Max/MSP, OpenMusic, and AudioSculpt.

nodes.label: CCRMA
nodes.description: Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics at Stanford. Founded by Chowning. Home of FM synthesis, physical modeling, and Faust.

nodes.label: MIT Media Lab
nodes.description: Where Barry Vercoe created Csound. Research lab exploring technology, multimedia, and human-computer interaction.

nodes.label: GRM
nodes.description: Groupe de Recherches Musicales. Founded by Pierre Schaeffer at French radio. Birthplace of musique concrète and acousmatic research.

nodes.label: WDR Studio
nodes.description: Westdeutscher Rundfunk electronic music studio in Cologne. Birthplace of elektronische Musik. Stockhausen's primary studio.

nodes.label: CNMAT
nodes.description: Center for New Music and Audio Technologies at UC Berkeley. Founded by David Wessel. Research in real-time performance and spatial audio.

nodes.label: Csound Community
nodes.description: Open-source community maintaining and developing Csound since its release. Active mailing list, GitHub, FLOSS manual.

nodes.label: MTG (UPF)
nodes.description: Music Technology Group at Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Barcelona. Founded by Xavier Serra. Research on spectral processing, MIR, and Freesound.

nodes.label: EAM Paris
nodes.description: Electroacoustic Music Studies at various Paris institutions. Hub for acousmatic and electroacoustic composition research.

nodes.label: Berklee College of Music
nodes.description: Home of the Electronic Production and Sound Design department. Richard Boulanger teaches Csound here.

nodes.label: Maynooth University
nodes.description: Victor Lazzarini's base. Major center for Csound development and music technology research.

nodes.label: Princeton
nodes.description: Home of the Princeton Sound Lab. Paul Lansky and Perry Cook's base for computer music and physical modeling research.

nodes.label: FM Synthesis
nodes.description: Frequency Modulation synthesis discovered by John Chowning in 1967. Uses one oscillator to modulate the frequency of another, producing complex spectra from simple components. Basis of the Yamaha DX7.

nodes.label: Granular Synthesis
nodes.description: Sound synthesis from thousands of tiny grains (1-100ms). Theorized by Gabor (1947), realized computationally by Roads and Xenakis. Used for time-stretching, spectral freezing, and texture creation.

nodes.label: Additive Synthesis
nodes.description: Building complex sounds by summing individual sine waves (partials). Based on Fourier's theorem. Risset's trumpet analysis was a landmark application.

nodes.label: Subtractive Synthesis
nodes.description: Starting with harmonically rich waveforms and filtering to shape timbre. Foundation of analog synthesizers (Moog, Buchla). Modeled digitally in Csound with moogvcf, butterlp, etc.

nodes.label: Physical Modeling
nodes.description: Simulating the physics of sound-producing mechanisms. Waveguide synthesis (Smith), modal synthesis, finite element methods. Produces realistic instrument sounds from physical equations.

nodes.label: Spectral Processing
nodes.description: Analyzing and manipulating sound in the frequency domain via FFT/STFT. Includes spectral morphing, cross-synthesis, spectral freezing. Serra's SMS was a landmark system.

nodes.label: Wavetable Synthesis
nodes.description: Storing one or more waveform cycles in a table and reading through them at variable rates. Foundation of most digital synthesis. Csound's GEN routines fill function tables.

nodes.label: Stochastic Synthesis
nodes.description: Using probability distributions and random processes to generate sound. Xenakis' GENDYN (1991) directly computed waveforms from stochastic functions.

nodes.label: Sample-Based Synthesis
nodes.description: Playback and manipulation of recorded audio samples. Includes looping, pitch-shifting, layering. Foundation of samplers (Fairlight CMI, Akai). Csound uses loscil, diskin2.

nodes.label: Ring Modulation
nodes.description: Multiplying two signals to produce sum and difference frequencies. Creates metallic, inharmonic timbres. Used extensively by Stockhausen.

nodes.label: Musique Concrète
nodes.description: Composition with recorded sounds (objets sonores) rather than traditional notes. Founded by Pierre Schaeffer in 1948 at RTF Paris.

nodes.label: Elektronische Musik
nodes.description: Pure electronic sound synthesis from oscillators and filters. Developed at WDR Cologne by Stockhausen, Eimert, and others. Counterpart to musique concrète.

nodes.label: Csound
nodes.description: Sound design programming language created by Barry Vercoe at MIT (1986). Descended from MUSIC-N lineage. Over 1500 opcodes. The most powerful open-source synthesis system.

nodes.label: Max/MSP
nodes.description: Visual programming environment for music and multimedia. Created by Miller Puckette at IRCAM (1988). MSP added real-time audio. Commercial version by Cycling '74.

nodes.label: Pure Data
nodes.description: Open-source visual programming language by Miller Puckette. Free alternative to Max/MSP. Used extensively in interactive art and education.

nodes.label: SuperCollider
nodes.description: Real-time audio synthesis programming language by James McCartney. Client-server architecture. Influential in live coding and algorithmic composition communities.

nodes.label: Faust
nodes.description: Functional Audio Stream language. DSP programming language that compiles to C++, WebAssembly, etc. Developed at GRAME. Used for plugin and embedded audio development.

nodes.label: MUSIC-N Family
nodes.description: The lineage of computer music languages starting with Max Mathews' MUSIC I (1957) through MUSIC V, leading to Csound, CMusic, CLM, and many others.

nodes.label: Ambisonics
nodes.description: Spatial audio technique encoding sound fields as spherical harmonics. Supports arbitrary speaker layouts and binaural rendering. Csound supports B-format and higher-order ambisonics.

nodes.label: FOF Synthesis
nodes.description: Fonction d'Onde Formantique — formant wave function synthesis for vocal sounds. Developed by Xavier Rodet at IRCAM. Models vowel formants without physical modeling.

nodes.label: Waveguide Synthesis
nodes.description: Physical modeling technique using delay lines to simulate wave propagation in strings, tubes, and membranes. Developed by Julius O. Smith III at CCRMA.

nodes.label: Cabbage
nodes.description: Framework by Rory Walsh for creating VST/AU/standalone audio plugins from Csound code. Auto-generates GUIs from a simple markup language.

nodes.label: CsoundQt
nodes.description: The primary IDE for Csound by Andrés Cabrera. Features code editor, widget panel, live coding, and built-in documentation.

nodes.label: Blue
nodes.description: Composition environment for Csound by Steven Yi. Supports timeline-based composition, SoundObjects, and Python scripting.

nodes.label: Web Audio API
nodes.description: Browser API for audio processing and synthesis. Enables Csound to run in web browsers via WebAssembly (@csound/browser). Foundation for web-based music apps.

nodes.label: MIDI
nodes.description: Musical Instrument Digital Interface. Standard protocol for communicating musical performance data. Adopted 1983. Extended by MIDI 2.0 (2020).

nodes.label: Gesang der Jünglinge
nodes.description: Stockhausen (1956). Landmark work combining electronic sounds with processed boy's voice. First major spatialized electronic composition.

nodes.label: Silver Apples of the Moon
nodes.description: Morton Subotnick (1967). First electronic music commissioned by a record label (Nonesuch). Created on Don Buchla's modular synthesizer.

nodes.label: Stria
nodes.description: John Chowning (1977). Masterwork of FM synthesis. Uses the golden ratio to determine frequency ratios, creating shimmering, otherworldly timbres.

nodes.label: Turenas
nodes.description: John Chowning (1972). First piece to use computer-controlled spatial sound movement. Pioneered the illusion of sound moving through 3D space.

nodes.label: Mutations
nodes.description: Jean-Claude Risset (1969). Demonstrates paradoxical Risset rhythms and tones — sounds that seem to endlessly accelerate or ascend.

nodes.label: Mild und Leise
nodes.description: Paul Lansky (1973). Computer-synthesized piece using LPC analysis of speech. Its textures influenced Radiohead's 'Everything in Its Right Place'.

nodes.label: Kontakte
nodes.description: Stockhausen (1960). Four-channel electronic composition exploring connections (Kontakte) between electronic and instrumental sound worlds.

nodes.label: Metastaseis
nodes.description: Xenakis (1954). Orchestral work using mathematical structures (hyperbolic paraboloids). Bridge from architecture to algorithmic composition.

nodes.label: GENDY3
nodes.description: Xenakis (1991). Pure stochastic synthesis — all sound generated from probability distributions. No oscillators, no samples, only mathematics.

nodes.label: Vox 5
nodes.description: Trevor Wishart (1986). Pioneering work of sound transformation, morphing human voice through a series of impossible metamorphoses.

nodes.label: Riverrun
nodes.description: Barry Truax (1986). Landmark granular synthesis composition. Sound flows like water from a single drop to a torrent and back.

nodes.label: Étude aux chemins de fer
nodes.description: Pierre Schaeffer (1948). The first musique concrète piece, composed from recordings of trains. Birth of electroacoustic music.

nodes.label: Paris
nodes.description: Home of IRCAM, GRM, and the musique concrète tradition. Central hub of electroacoustic music research since 1948.

nodes.label: Stanford
nodes.description: Home of CCRMA. Where FM synthesis was invented and physical modeling synthesis was developed.

nodes.label: Murray Hill, NJ
nodes.description: Location of Bell Labs where Max Mathews created the first computer music in 1957.

nodes.label: Cologne
nodes.description: Home of the WDR electronic music studio. Birthplace of elektronische Musik in the 1950s.

nodes.label: Cambridge, MA
nodes.description: Home of MIT, where Barry Vercoe created Csound at the MIT Media Lab.

nodes.label: Fourier's Theorem
nodes.description: Any periodic waveform can be decomposed into a sum of sine waves. Foundation of spectral analysis, additive synthesis, and FFT-based processing.

nodes.label: Nyquist-Shannon Theorem
nodes.description: A continuous signal can be perfectly reconstructed from samples if sampled at twice its highest frequency. Foundation of digital audio.

nodes.label: Unit Generator
nodes.description: Modular building block for computer music (oscillator, filter, envelope, etc.). Concept from Mathews' MUSIC III. Csound opcodes are unit generators.

nodes.label: Objet Sonore
nodes.description: Schaeffer's 'sound object' — a segment of sound perceived as a unified whole, independent of its source. Foundation of acousmatic listening.

nodes.label: Spectromorphology
nodes.description: Denis Smalley's framework for describing sound shapes through spectral and morphological features. Key analytical tool for electroacoustic music.

nodes.label: Acousmatic Listening
nodes.description: Listening to sound without seeing its source. Derived from Pythagoras via Schaeffer. Foundation of electroacoustic concert tradition.

nodes.label: Stochastic Music
nodes.description: Xenakis' approach: using probability theory and statistical mechanics to compose music. Gaussian distributions, Markov chains, random walks.

nodes.label: Live Coding
nodes.description: Performance practice of writing and modifying code in real-time to generate music. Communities include TOPLAP, Algorave. Supported by SuperCollider, Csound, Sonic Pi.

nodes.label: Sonification
nodes.description: Mapping non-audio data to sound for analysis or artistic purposes. Weather, seismic, financial, and biological data have all been sonified.

nodes.label: Microsound
nodes.description: Curtis Roads' framework for composition at the micro time scale (samples to grains). Explores the continuum from individual samples to sound masses.

nodes.label: Yamaha DX7
nodes.description: The best-selling synthesizer of the 1980s. Based on Chowning's FM synthesis patent licensed from Stanford. Defined the sound of a decade.

nodes.label: Voyager Golden Record
nodes.description: Launched 1977. Contains Laurie Spiegel's Kepler's Harmony of the World, one of the first computer music works sent into interstellar space.

nodes.label: ICMC
nodes.description: International Computer Music Conference. Annual gathering of the computer music community since 1974. Organized by ICMA.

nodes.label: NIME
nodes.description: New Interfaces for Musical Expression. Annual conference exploring new ways to interact with music technology. Founded 2001.

nodes.label: DAFx
nodes.description: Digital Audio Effects conference. Annual conference on audio signal processing and effects. Running since 1998.
